title: From Non-secure World to Secure World

c.v: Figure 16.4-2 shows
main()
in the Non-secure World with
ENTRY_ADDR(X)
set to the entry address of Function B and
ENTRY_CHECK=1<<X
; Function B then runs in the Secure World ("configuration" followed by "Entry Secure World").

blocks.alt: Figure 16.4-2. Switching From Non-secure World to Secure World
blocks.caption: Figure 16.4-2. Switching From Non-secure World to Secure World

c.v: CPU can only switch from Non-secure World to Secure World via Interrupts (or Exceptions).
After configuring the World Controller, the CPU can switch back Non-secure World to Secure World upon the configured Interrupt trigger.
See details below:
Configure Registers WCL_CORE_m_MESSAGE_ADDR_REG and WCL_CORE_m_MESSAGE_MAX_REG to clear write_buffer, as described in
Section 16.4.3
Configure Registers WCL_CORE_m_ENTRY_n_ADDR_REG (n: 1-13) as the entry address of interrupts (or exceptions).
Note that all of ESP32-S3's interrupts and exceptions are using VecBase + offset as its address.
Therefore, you need to configure WCL_CORE_m_ENTRY_n_ADDR_REG (n: 1-13) whenever you modify the VecBase.
Configure Register WCL_CORE_m_ENTRY_CHECK_REG to enable the monitor of a certain entry.
In this way, the CPU switches to the Secure World immediately when it executes the address monitored at this particular entry.
Bit x controls the entry monitoring of Entry x (WCL_CORE_m_ENTRY_x_ADDR_REG).
You can enable monitoring for more than one entry.
0: Disable monitoring
1: Enable monitoring
Register WCL_CORE_m_ENTRY_CHECK_REG is effective after configuration all the time till it's disabled, meaning you don't need to configure this register every time after each world switch.
